newsitem.title: USA: Exide's Reading lead smelter workers strike.
newsitem.headline: Exide's Reading lead smelter workers strike.

text.p: Exide Corp said workers at its lead smelter in Reading, Pa., rejected the union's recommendation to accept a new pay deal and went on strike.
Last Friday, United Steelworkers of America negotiators and Exide reached a tentative agreement on a new pay deal for the 116 workers at the lead recycling plant.
But on May 11, union members voted 56 to 49 to reject the deal and walked out, an Exide spokeswoman said. She was unable to say if the smelter was still operating.
The auto-battery making plant and distribution center at the facility were not affected, the company spokeswoman added.
But Gerald Waldbiesser, president of Local 5227 of USW involved in the dispute, said the smelter shut on Monday.
"I have been told the company will bring foremen and clerks from other smelters and they have plans to restart the operation tomorrow," Waldbiesser said.
Production at the smelter, which remelts lead from spent auto batteries, is 93,000 short tons a year, Waldbiesser believed.
Further negotiations between the union and the company were due Friday when a mediator would take part, though he had no powers to order workers back to the plant, Waldbiesser said.
The tentative new three-year deal offered a $1.10 per hour pay hike over the life of the agreement, but the workers want $1.50 hike, Waldbiesser said.
Exide is the world's biggest auto lead-acid battery maker and has several lead recycling smelters in the U.S. and Europe.
Traders have said the market is locked in a seasonal lull at the moment with spot demand modest.
The Exide spokeswoman said the company would be able to bring in lead from other plants if needed.
